sources: Authored in-house for three.ws on 2026-11-16. Queries and passages are original text written for this set; no dataset, documentation or third-party text was copied.
notes: Retrieval over a small corpus. Each query has exactly one relevant passage; the other passages include hard distractors that share its vocabulary. Queries are embedded with input_type=query and passages with input_type=passage, then ranked by cosine similarity. Quality is recall@1; MRR is reported alongside.

passages.text: Auto-rigging adds a humanoid skeleton and skin weights to a static mesh so it can be posed and animated without manual weight painting.
A static mesh exported without a skeleton can still be lit, textured and rendered, but it cannot bend at the joints.
GLB is the binary container for glTF: the JSON scene description, the vertex buffers and the textures are packed into one file.
A glTF file can reference external PNG textures and a separate .bin buffer, which is convenient when editing assets by hand.
Audio-driven facial animation predicts blendshape weights from speech so an avatar's mouth moves in time with the voice.
Blendshapes can also be keyed by hand in an animation tool, which gives an artist full control over every expression.
A custodial wallet is held by the platform on the user's behalf, so the user does not manage a seed phrase themselves.
Hardware wallets keep private keys on a separate device and require a physical button press to approve each transaction.
When a free inference endpoint answers 429, the client should back off and route the request to the next provider in its fallback chain.
A 404 response means the requested resource does not exist, so retrying the same request will not help.
Embedding vectors from two different models live in different spaces and cannot be compared, so stored vectors are tagged with the model that produced them.
Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors and ignores their length, which suits normalised embeddings.
A GPU service that scales to zero pays a cold start on the first request, because the container and the model weights must load before it can answer.
Keeping one instance warm costs idle GPU time but removes the delay for users who arrive after a quiet period.
Before a generation slot is spent, the uploaded photo is screened for problems such as a screenshot of text, a cluttered scene, or an image that is too dark.
Photographers often shoot in raw format so they can recover detail in dark areas of the image during editing.
Level of detail swaps a high-polygon mesh for simpler versions as the camera moves away, keeping the frame rate steady in large scenes.
Increasing the polygon count of a model makes curved surfaces look smoother when the camera is close.
OpenUSD describes a scene as layers that can be composed and overridden, which lets several tools edit the same stage without overwriting each other.
Exporting a scene to a single flattened file is simpler to share but loses the ability to override individual layers later.
Text-to-speech turns written text into audio; multilingual voices let one avatar speak several languages with the same identity.
Speech recognition converts spoken audio into text so a voice command can be handled like a typed message.
A cross-encoder reranker reads the query and each candidate passage together and re-scores the top results so the most relevant context comes first.
Keyword search ranks documents by how often the query terms appear, which misses passages that use different words for the same idea.
